1 Bُ , (S, M, A, Msb, K,) aor. بَثْرٌ, (Msb,) inf. n. بُثُورٌ; (M, Msb, K;) and بَثُرَ, (S, M, Msb, K,) aor.
بََُثَ , (S, M, Msb,) inf. n. بَثْرٌ (M, Msb, K) and بُثُورٌ; (M, K;) and بَثُرٌ, aor.
بََُثَ ; (S, Msb, K;) It (a man's face, S, M, K, or the skin, M, A, Msb) broke out with pimples, or small pustules; (S, M, A, Msb, K;) as also ↓ تبثّر : (M, A, and some copies of the K:) or this last signifies it (a man's skin) became blistered, or vesicated. (S, Msb.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
